# Executive summary

This report evaluates Keir's proposed log-scale retransformation correction
across the six shortlisted Yang–Zhang volatility models. For each model, the
target is fit as $Z_t=\log(Y_t)$, then forecasts are returned to the volatility
scale using

$$
\widehat{Y}_{t+1}
= \exp\left(\widehat{\mu}_{t+1}
  + \frac{1}{2}\widehat{\sigma}_{t+1}^{\,2}\right).
$$

The correction estimates the conditional mean if log-scale forecast errors are
conditionally normal. By contrast, $\exp(\widehat{\mu}_{t+1})$ estimates the
conditional median. The experiment used 761 sequential holdout targets from
2023-06-02 through 2026-11-10, with zero failed fits across all six models.

The transformation did **not** resolve the larger Q5 errors. On the exact
baseline-Q5 dates, raw residual variance rose for five models and fell by only
0.2% for HGB. None of the paired overall MAE or RMSE differences was
significant at 5% after Holm adjustment. Treat the results as an exploratory
comparison on a previously used holdout, not as evidence of a winning model.

# Data and model implementation

The target is the unannualized daily volatility, the square root of the
two-observation Yang–Zhang variance estimate from LSEG's generic COMEX gold
futures series `GCc1`. The chronological sample has 3,040 training targets and
761 test targets. At each test origin, fitting used the initial training
sample and only previously observed test targets; the target being forecast
was excluded from its own history.

The six models were:

| Model | Log-scale specification and variance used for correction |
|:--|:--|
| GARCH(1,1) | AR(1) mean and GARCH(1,1) conditional variance, fit to log volatility |
| EGARCH(1,1) | AR(1) mean and EGARCH(1,1) conditional variance, fit to log volatility |
| Range GARCH-X | AR(1) log-volatility mean; OHLC range enters the conditional-variance equation; Gaussian quasi-likelihood |
| EGARCH-X | Selected DXY and gold implied-volatility predictors remain in the ARX mean; EGARCH conditional variance |
| HAR-X (OHLC) | Existing HAR lag and predictor regression on log volatility; training OLS residual variance |
| HGB (OHLC) | Existing log-target boosting specification; training in-sample residual variance; random seed 42 |

HAR-X and HGB already model log volatility in the existing pipeline. For
these models, this experiment applies the variance correction; the other four
models are refit on the log target. GARCH-family corrections use the fitted
one-step conditional log variance. Regression-model corrections use
training-sample log-residual variance. HGB's in-sample residual variance may
understate its prediction error.

# Overall holdout performance

Errors are defined as **actual minus forecast**; positive mean error denotes
under-forecasting. Metrics are shown in units of $10^{-3}$ volatility.

| Model | MAE: baseline → corrected | RMSE: baseline → corrected | Mean error: baseline → corrected |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| GARCH(1,1) | 2.912 → 2.930 | 5.025 → 5.036 | 0.644 → 0.420 |
| EGARCH(1,1) | 2.912 → 2.945 | 5.022 → 5.115 | 0.621 → 0.540 |
| Range GARCH-X | 2.914 → 2.930 | 5.037 → 5.036 | 0.716 → 0.420 |
| EGARCH-X | 2.833 → 2.855 | 4.860 → 4.902 | 0.321 → 0.086 |
| HAR-X (OHLC) | 2.758 → 2.825 | 5.625 → 5.852 | 0.623 → −0.060 |
| HGB (OHLC) | 2.423 → 2.437 | 4.736 → 4.657 | 0.821 → 0.386 |

The mean bias moved closer to zero for all six models, but the point-loss
changes were small and mixed. HGB's RMSE decreased slightly; its Holm-adjusted
DM p-value was 0.058 with Newey–West bandwidth 1 and 0.142 with bandwidth 4.
Neither is below 0.05. No model's overall paired MAE or RMSE difference was
significant after adjustment.

# Q5 residual variance

The first variance comparison below holds Q5 membership fixed to the baseline
model's highest forecast quintile, so both forecast versions are evaluated on
the same 152 dates. Variances are in units of $10^{-5}$ volatility squared.
The last column reports the corrected forecast's own Q5/Q1 error-variance
ratio, with quintiles ranked within that model over the holdout.

| Model | Baseline Q5 variance | Corrected variance on same dates | Variance change | Corrected model Q5/Q1 |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| GARCH(1,1) | 7.433 | 7.543 | +1.5% | 9.65 |
| EGARCH(1,1) | 7.437 | 7.839 | +5.4% | 9.90 |
| Range GARCH-X | 7.441 | 7.543 | +1.4% | 9.65 |
| EGARCH-X | 7.288 | 7.600 | +4.3% | 15.53 |
| HAR-X (OHLC) | 11.413 | 12.881 | +12.9% | 20.93 |
| HGB (OHLC) | 7.038 | 7.024 | −0.2% | 13.27 |

Thus, the log transformation and mean correction did not make high-forecast
errors less dispersed. The Q5/Q1 ratios remain substantially above one. The
variance changes are descriptive; no separate statistical test of Q5 variance
differences was performed.

# Paired forecast-loss tests

For each model, corrected forecasts were compared with that model's existing
baseline on the same target dates. Tests use absolute and squared errors,
Newey–West bandwidths 1 and 4, the Harvey–Leybourne–Newbold correction, and
Holm adjustment across the six model comparisons within each loss/bandwidth
family. Negative transformed-minus-baseline loss favors the corrected
forecast.

No overall comparison is statistically significant at the 5% level after
Holm adjustment. The closest result is HGB squared error: adjusted p-values
are 0.058 (bandwidth 1) and 0.142 (bandwidth 4). Full statistics are in the
[DM results CSV](../outputs/samuel/stage3_q5/log_transform/log_transform_dm_tests.csv).

# Limitations and interpretation

- The retransformation formula is exact under a conditional normal
  log-error model. Normality has not been established for HAR-X or HGB.
- HAR-X uses training OLS residual variance; HGB uses in-sample residual
  variance, which may be optimistic.
- The holdout has been used in prior model analysis. Forecast-ranked Q5 is
  retrospective, and adjacent two-observation Yang–Zhang targets overlap.
- Paired tests concern overall loss, not Q5 variance. The same-holdout
  comparisons are exploratory and do not establish causal effects or durable
  superiority.
- Lower mean error does not by itself establish full forecast calibration.
